Meet the Wilts
​

Sublime Organics, LLC is owned and operated by Greg and Ellen Wilt.  The farm-business was established in 2014 and certified as organic by Oregon Tilth in 2015.  Sweet Pea, a purebred border collie, is our stalwart companion and in 2018 she gave birth to eight puppies, two of which stayed with our family.

Meats

Certified Organic Katahdin lamb meat  is high-quality, tender, and sweet meat. Not gamey.  Our livestock are raised in pasture grass all their lives, and are treated humanely and in an ecologically sustainable manner. Our farming practices are guided by biodynamic principles.

Livestock and Hay

 

 

Here is what you need to know: USDA Certified Organic, organically raised, naturally grown, and no spray products differ. Read on.

​​

 USDA Certified Organic products must pass a rigorous certification process, ensuring that farming practices comply with the National Organics Program (NOP). The NOP specifies the materials and practices that must be followed to obtain certification (such as synthetic chemical-free applications and conservation practices). Annual inspections ensure such compliance.

,

Organically raised, naturally grown and no spray products may or may not follow the same or similar wholesome and synthetic chemical-free practices. We encourage you to ask farmers how their products are grown/raised.

 

Sublime Organics offers high-quality meats that are either USDA Certified Organic or organically raised. Our USDA Certified Organic and organically raised livestock graze side-by-side on USDA Certified Organic pasture grass and are fed USDA Certified Organic hay and GMO-free grains. None of our livestock receive growth hormones. Organically raised livestock received one or more medications to treat illness during their lifetime. If those medications were not specified in the NOP, those animals do not qualify as USDA Certified Organic.

​

All of our livestock have been certified Animal Welfare Approved (AWA). An AWA certification by A Greener World, guarantees animals are raised outdoors on pasture or range for their entire lives on an independent farm using truly sustainable, high-welfare farming practices. Annual inspections ensure compliance.

Our farm, which is entirely Certified Organic by Oregon Tilth, is 67 acres in total. We cultivate market vegetables on about 4 acres per year. In addition to our fruit orchard, we harvest raspberries and wild blackberries for market sales and for making delicious preserves. We raise Boer goats, Katahdin sheep, and Muskovey ducks for meat and eggs. In addition, the livestock contribute to the biodynamics of this farm by generating a plethora of fertilizer and by keeping weeds and nuisance insects at bay as they graze and forage. We are proud of our conservation efforts on the forested watershed and wetlands on the property, and we plant native vegetation that attracts and sustains native pollinators.

How We Get All That Work Done!

Greg and Ellen would not be able to produce fine fruits and vegetables, care for livestock, and steward their lands if not for the assistance of volunteers through Worldwide Opportunities On Organic Farms (WWOOF).  Across the years, Greg and Ellen have hosted dozens of folks eager to work outside, put their hands in the dirt, and learn about organic farming practices.  Because no herbicides are used on the farm, many hours of labor are spent pulling weeds.  Primarily three invasive exotic weeds plague the farmlands: tansy ragwort, which can sicken or kill livestock, Scotch broom, and Bull thistle.
